name: Petra — Al-Khazneh
scaleNote: 1 stud per metre. The Treasury's six lower columns are the shot; they have to be more than one stud thick.

interiorVolume.source: Wikipedia, Al-Khazneh: 'an interior volume of around 2,000 m3 (71,000 cu ft)' for the main chamber and three antechambers.

note:
ONE CITED FIGURE, AND IT IS A VOLUME. Wikipedia's Al-Khazneh article gives the interior volume and no facade dimension at all -- no height, no width, no column height. The commonly repeated 39 m x 25 m is not in the article read for this sheet, so it is not in `dimensions` and every figure in this massing is counted as the modeller's.

That is a worse ratio than Machu Picchu's. If the Atlas ships Petra it ships a proportioned guess at a rock-cut facade, and this note is the disclosure. A dimensioned survey of Al-Khazneh would fix it in one edit.

WHAT IT IS: two storeys of Colonnade cut into a Wall face, which is what a rock-cut facade is -- a wall with an order in front of it.
